intended_prior_behavior_changes: For 18.10.0, an invoked exchange followed by 503 or ambiguous response loss no longer authorizes a same-generation resend; the credential row remains healthy and unchanged while the attempt fails closed.

Known replacements may be staged after timeout or lease loss and published by a later owner without another exchange. Nonrotating staging references the existing refresh secret rather than duplicating R0.

Broker results are authoritative complete rows, including intentional field absence. Actual managed MCP and failure-fallback consumers must not restore captured pre-await metadata or bearer bytes after logout.
Automatic delegated refresh failures cannot become unconditional broker disable operations; explicit user disable remains functional.
Writable transfer/adoption and rollback preserve ownership and artifacts. Read-only replicas cannot synthesize eval, repair, model or memory metadata.
Successful same-path reloads must invalidate outgoing recall ownership even when only recall metadata changes and displayed messages remain identical.

assertions: The original A request returns null and performs zero usage-provider probes after the row changes to identity B.
A retained legacy A quota cannot reappear; neither canonical nor legacy A cache keys may contain A or B report data after the identity-changing request.
